# Laheeb Atlas Project

## Data Management, Data Integrity & Reporting Accuracy — Change Requests

### Purpose

The following requests are not only interface edits. They are important operational and strategic requirements for Laheeb Atlas because they directly affect:

* Accuracy of historical reports
* Reliability of cost, profit, inventory, and order calculations
* Data consistency across the application
* Customer and product traceability
* Ability to scale the system without manual errors
* Management's trust in the numbers generated by the system

These changes should be treated as **core data architecture and business logic requirements**, not minor UI changes.

---

## 1. Date Format Standardization

**Requirement:** Change the date format across the whole system to **DD/MM/YYYY** (e.g. `08/06/2026`) instead of formats where the month appears before the day.

**Strategic Importance:** Wrong date formatting can cause serious confusion in orders, inventory records, production batches, financial reports, and historical analysis.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
* All displayed dates must use **DD/MM/YYYY**.
* All date filters, order dates, invoice dates, inventory dates, batch dates, and report dates must follow the same format.
* The database can store dates in standard ISO format internally, but the UI must display them as **DD/MM/YYYY**.

---

## 2. Full Editability of Orders in Data Management

**Requirement:** Inside **Orders Data Management**, the user must be able to fully edit order information: update order details, add/delete items, edit item quantity, edit item price, item-level discount, order-level discount, extras/custom charges, custom fields/notes, edit linked customer info, and delete/update wrong information (by permission). Any change must automatically update all related calculations.

**Required Auto-Calculations:** subtotal, discounts, extras, delivery fee, final invoice total, product quantities sold, inventory deductions, revenue reports, gross profit reports, customer purchase history, related dashboard numbers.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
* User can add, remove, or edit items inside an existing order.
* User can edit quantity, discount, extras, and notes.
* Invoice total updates automatically after every change.
* Related reports and dashboards update accordingly.
* The system keeps an edit history / audit log (what changed, when, by whom).
* Sensitive edits controlled by permission level.

---

## 3. Historical Cost and Price Protection

**Problem:** If the cost of a product, raw material, or packaging changes and we update it in the system, this must **not affect old historical reports**. Example: packaging cost 500 IQD in May → 650 IQD in June; May reports must keep using 500 IQD.

**Requirement:** Support **cost and price versioning**. Changing cost/price affects only future transactions. Applies to: finished products, raw coffee beans, packaging, labels, boxes, sachets, cups, any inventory item used in cost calculation.

**Recommended Solution:**
* **Option A — Effective Date Versioning:** each cost/price record has item ID, value, start date, end date (if replaced), active/inactive. Reports use the cost active on the transaction date.
* **Option B — Transaction Snapshot:** when an order/batch/inventory movement is created, save a snapshot of the cost at that time.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
* Updating a product/raw-material/packaging cost does not change old reports/batches/orders.
* Future orders and batches use the new cost.
* Reports calculated from the cost valid at the transaction time.
* The system shows cost history per item.

---

## 4. Customer ID Auto-Generation and Protection

**Current Issue:** Customer ID is entered manually (`CL-1`, `CL-2`). This should become automatic.

**Requirement:** Auto-generate a unique customer ID, suggested format `CL-000001`. The ID appears beside the customer name.

**Required Behavior:** auto-generated; not manually entered; not duplicable; not editable after creation; fixed forever; searchable; appears in profile, table, orders, invoices, reports.

**Acceptance Criteria:** new ID auto-generated; not editable after creation; duplicates disallowed; searchable by ID; appears beside name; linked to all orders/reports.

---

## 5. Protect Unique IDs Across the System

**Requirement:** Same ID protection for: Customer ID, Product ID, Inventory item ID, Raw material ID, Packaging material ID, Batch ID, Order/Invoice ID.

**Required Behavior:** auto-generated where possible; unique; not duplicated; not editable after creation; used as the permanent reference.

**Acceptance Criteria:** IDs cannot be duplicated; cannot be manually changed after creation; uniqueness validated before saving; related records stay connected through fixed IDs.

---

## 6. Customer Profile Fields

**Requirement:** Add to the customer profile: Customer ID, name, phone, city, Address 1, street details, customer source, notes.

**Customer Source Field options:** Instagram, Facebook, Website, WhatsApp, Referral, Offline, Manual entry, Other.

**Acceptance Criteria:** city/address1/street/source available; appear in the customer table where needed; customer ID beside name.

---

## 7. Add Customer Address to Invoice

**Requirement:** Invoice shows customer name, customer ID, phone, city, Address 1, street details.

**Acceptance Criteria:** invoice displays the address clearly; updates automatically if linked order/customer details change; clear/readable format.

---

## 8. Order Item Editing and Invoice Reflection

**Requirement:** When editing order items, the invoice reflects all changes (product/item, quantity, discount, extras, notes, custom additions, removed items).

**Acceptance Criteria:** added items appear; removed items disappear; quantity changes update; discounts/extras appear clearly; totals recalculate automatically.

---

## 9. Search, Filter, and Sort in Data Management

**Requirement:** Add search, filter, and sort to all Data Management sections: Orders, Customers, Products, Inventory items, Raw materials, Packaging materials, Batches, any searchable table.

**Search by:** Order ID, invoice number, customer ID, customer name, phone, product ID, product name, amount, date, city, source, any important field.

**Filter by:** date range, customer, city, product, order status, payment status, source, amount range, inventory category, product category.

**Sort by:** newest/oldest, highest/lowest amount, customer name, city, product name, quantity, status.

**Acceptance Criteria:** search/filter/sort available across Orders, Customers, Products, Inventory and major tables; works by ID, name, phone, date, amount; fast and accurate.

---

## 10. Recommended Priority

**Priority 1 — Critical** (data accuracy & system trust):
1. Historical cost and price protection
2. Auto-generated and protected IDs
3. Full order editability with recalculation
4. Search, filter, and sort in data management

**Priority 2 — High** (operational usability):
1. Customer profile fields
2. Customer address on invoice
3. Invoice update after order item edits
4. Customer source field

**Priority 3 — Medium** (consistency & UX):
1. Date format standardization
2. Visual table display improvements
3. Showing customer ID beside customer name

---

## 11. General Development Notes

Avoid overwriting historical data unless the user clearly intends to correct a mistake. For important edits (orders, costs, inventory) keep an audit trail showing: previous value, new value, user, date/time, related record. Laheeb Atlas is a management system, not only a data entry tool.

---

## Final Note

These changes are required to make Laheeb Atlas reliable for real business operations — protecting the accuracy of reports, historical records, customer information, inventory calculations, and financial decisions.
